**Indikator 4y** is a supplementary national quality indicator for acute surgery that measures the proportion of patients with ileus surgery—without ischemia or perforation—who are operated on within 24 hours of hospital arrival [^src1]. It addresses a less acute, but still time-critical, patient group that requires structured monitoring to ensure timely care [^src1]. The indicator is calculated using data from the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] [^src1]. It specifically measures [[behandlingshastighed-ileus|behandlingshastighed-ileus]] (treatment speed for ileus) [^src2]. The official indicator descriptions and annual evaluations are published by the [[sundhedsvaesenets-kvalitetsinstitut|Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut]] as part of a broader national effort to monitor quality, compare regional performance, and support evidence-based prioritization in acute surgery [^src1].

The most recent measurement period for Indikator 4y spanned from September 1, 2023, to August 31, 2024 [^src1]. During this period, the national result for the indicator was 82.6% (95% CI: 80.6–84.4), meaning that 82.6% of the targeted patients were operated on within the 24-hour window [^src1]. This performance did not meet the established development goal of ≥ 90% [^src1]. The annual results and their implications are actively discussed to identify systemic challenges, such as operating room capacity, and to guide future clinical practices and resource allocation [^src2].
